name: Viktor Reise
caption: A German heavyweight billed as BodyCount's own national hero, who won every bout of the first Warrior Grand Prix by knockout or stoppage to become its first champion.

tenures.source: BodyCount's own list of participants (23 August 2012) and its round-by-round Warrior Grand Prix results columns, all served

name: Jakob Alexander
caption: A middleweight billed 'Weapon X,' who won three straight Warrior Grand Prix bouts by decision, submission-defense and knockout before falling to Viktor Reise in the tournament's final.

tenures.source: BodyCount's own list of participants (23 August 2012), its round-by-round Warrior Grand Prix results columns and a hype promo exchange with Mike Sodo (22-23 September 2012), all served

name: Dave Hendrix
caption: A middleweight who upset the tournament's largest competitor with a leg-lock submission in the Warrior Grand Prix's third round, then lost his place in the final after the fed's own finals recap says he failed a drug test.

tenures.source: BodyCount's own list of participants (23 August 2012) and its Round 1-3 and finals Warrior Grand Prix results columns, all served

name: Jonathan Stark
caption: A middleweight billed 'Mutant X,' who won his first two Warrior Grand Prix bouts by knockout before losing a back-and-forth third-round decision to Jakob Alexander.

tenures.source: BodyCount's own list of participants (23 August 2012), its Round 2-3 Warrior Grand Prix results columns, and a cancelled qualifying-match notice (6 October 2012) not served

name: Michael Vayne
caption: A heavyweight boxer-wrestler who won his Warrior Grand Prix debut by knockout and advanced directly to the semifinals on the strength of it.

tenures.source: BodyCount's own entrance-music thread (5 September 2012) and its Round 1 Warrior Grand Prix results column, served; a semifinal promo thread against Dave Hendrix (opening 6 October 2012) survives but is not served, and no result for that bout survives anywhere in the held record

name: Mike Sodo
caption: A middleweight submission specialist billed 'The Torch,' who broke an opponent's arm in thirty seconds to open the Warrior Grand Prix before falling to Jakob Alexander on a split decision in round two.

tenures.source: BodyCount's own tournament-information post (22 August 2012, naming him as an early entrant), its Round 1-2 Warrior Grand Prix results columns, and a hype promo exchange with Jakob Alexander (22-23 September 2012), all served

name: Johannes Antonious de Castonovo
caption: A heavyweight billed 'the Adriatic Gargoyle,' eliminated in the Warrior Grand Prix's first round but reinstated on a golden ticket, then knocked out in the second round by a front kick.

tenures.source: BodyCount's own list of participants (23 August 2012), a backstory roleplay ('A Chronicle of the Adriatic Gargoyle,' 13 September 2012) and its Round 1-2 Warrior Grand Prix results columns, all served
